title: Client-side span aggregator and thresholded flush for high-throughput inference
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Problem: High QPS short-lived inference requests create large numbers of tiny spans that increase collector load and backend cost, and add noise to latency/error dashboards. Goal: implement a client-side lightweight span aggregator in SDKs that accrues short spans and emits aggregated spans on threshold (count/bytes/time) while preserving traceability for distributed traces.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a stable configuration for span aggregation with three knobs: max_spans, max_span_bytes, max_duration_ms
Aggregated spans are unrolled in the collector with preserved parent/trace IDs for end-to-end stitching
No measurable tail-latency regression for p50/p95 when aggregation is enabled (within 2% of baseline)
Collector ingestion rate reduced for synthetic high-QPS workload by >=40% in internal perf test
E2E tests added for W3C and B3 propagation compatibility and for fallback-to-immediate-flush when SLO tag present
technical_decisions: Design: client-side accumulator keeps proto-lite span fragments and emits a composite span with count/summary attributes rather than concatenating full stack traces
Propagation: keep original traceparent/x-b3 headers on first aggregated span; include a lightweight 'rspan' header to indicate aggregation metadata for downstream services
Sampling: respect root sampling decision; if sampled=false, only emit minimal aggregation metrics, not full payload
Flush policy: hybrid thresholds (count OR size OR time) and an immediate flush override for requests marked 'priority' via request context
Compatibility: implement in core JS/Go SDKs first; middleware adapters for Express/gRPC will be thin wrappers to set request context and priority flags
notes: This is different from server-side batching — intent is to reduce observability overhead before network egress and collector CPU cycles
Will require a small additive metric for 'aggregated_span_emitted' and a gauge for 'outstanding_aggregation_count' in SDK metrics
Security: ensure no sensitive PII gets aggregated into composite attributes; follow existing scrubbers in SDK pipeline
Telemetry contract: we will add a lightweight schema version header to aggregated payloads so the collector can gracefully migrate behavior
